action: Trace authored worklight placements to sector spawning and the everyday picker.
observation: The Helios Half-Shift cluster contains one tower; the Vesta faction berth spawns two subject to anchor and placement exclusion; Pallas counterweight defines two persistent fixtures. Everyday station-kit dressing selects at most one per sector. The separate Ceres occupational-yard table has no source caller.
decision: Treat the tower as an active but locally sparse prop, and do not count the disconnected occupational-yard row as a live copy.
next: Observe the actual gameplay footprint and nearby tower instances before prioritizing a performance intervention.
evidenceScope: current source tracing, not a player encounter
performance: No runtime draw, frame-time or visible instance count measured.

action: Count release-GLB geometry and inspect Forge floodhead and LOD authorship.
observation: The release contains 16,082 LOD0, 6,296 LOD1 and 2,693 LOD2 triangles apart from the hidden 282-triangle collider. The warm-light primitive stays at 1,984 triangles at LOD1 versus LOD0, falling to 810 at LOD2; eight floodheads each begin with 18-segment can, bezel, lens and halo components.
decision: Prioritize the unchanged middle-tier crown for an appearance-preserving candidate, but keep all eight lamp directions, silhouette and nav hooks until tested visually.
next: Compare camera-relevant angles and all tiers before specifying a geometry change to an Astra model author.
evidenceScope: current GLB data and Forge source; no rendered image
performance: Triangle counts are resource counts only, not measured frame time or draw calls.

action: Trace the tower's emissive materials and local light owners.
observation: The eight flood assemblies are emissive geometry. Ordinary world dressing rows default to fx and the spawner provides no Nocturne override; the Nocturne resolver does not automatically classify fx. The separate UI stage explicitly places practical lighting beside its tower.
decision: Do not delete or flatten the emissive crown on the assumption it creates eight dynamic lights; preserve UI-stage lighting when modifying geometry.
next: Inspect illuminated player-camera appearance and separately profile any actual admitted local lights.
evidenceScope: current source tracing; source-specific lighting, no runtime census
performance: No light-source or GPU timing sample collected.

action: Trace authored-place LOD selection, static batching and release material textures.
observation: Place roots initialize at LOD0, then the stable boundary may switch tiers based on projected size with hysteresis. Forge combines each tier by material; the place composer can further batch opaque leaves and keep nav nodes separate. The release has six KTX2 panel/machinery albedo, normal and ORM images, and its materials are opaque and single-sided.
decision: Preserve shared material maps and light hooks; do not assume nine raw node rows are nine separate draw calls or that two place owners are instanced.
next: Measure real package draw behavior and compare all tier silhouettes through the game renderer.
evidenceScope: source and GLB data; no live frame or texture memory measurement
performance: No draw-call or GPU timing sample collected.

action: Inspect existing historical top, close and chase views of the released tower.
observation: In an older top view the crown reads as four pairs of warm crescents surrounding a central amber beacon; at older chase framing the eight lamp details merge into one small lit crown while the yellow lattice, red nav markers and dark base remain the dominant shape. The older inspection view clips the head, so it cannot validate the complete silhouette.
decision: Preserve the lit crown's overall outline and warm-versus-amber hierarchy; a bounded lamp-mesh reduction is worth comparing at current close and chase scales, not deleting whole quadrants.
next: Inspect the queued current multi-angle baseline and review lower tiers before accepting geometry changes.
evidenceScope: historical isolated captures from October 24 and November 1, not the current renderer or ordinary gameplay
performance: No performance data accompanies these images.

action: Trace the Breakwater Spur-specific light owner and run a small scene-graph/origin experiment.
observation: Breakwater creates up to four real PointLights, one at the tower head, and admits two, three and four visible lights at restoration stages one, two and three. Its group coordinates remain galactic-global: at the actual Ceres site and snapped frame origin the head is at (-13538,16,6556) instead of frame-local (-1250,16,-1636); another origin change leaves it unshifted.
decision: Fix the presentation group's frame-local position in its own owner before judging the intended site illumination; do not mistake these lights for part of the tower model or remove them blindly.
next: Coordinate a presentation-owner correction and compare staged, rebased gameplay pictures.
evidenceScope: current source plus isolated scene-graph/coordinate probe, not a rendered player encounter
performance: The test counted visible scene lights; it did not measure frame time or prove a gameplay hitch.

action: Compare Breakwater's four staged lamps with the fixed NOCTURNE point-light director.
observation: The desktop NOCTURNE runtime has three physical point slots and competes logical sources by frustum, priority and distance; a synthetic stage-three selection has four valid site candidates and only three active. Disabling the director zeros its lamps, and mobile does not instantiate this runtime. The current Breakwater lights use direct Three PointLights instead.
decision: Do not migrate all four lamps into the existing three-slot pool as an equivalent optimization without nearby-image and disabled/mobile compatibility comparisons; distance-based visible toggles also alter Three's baked shader-light count.
next: Measure a bounded candidate at the site and far away after the coordinate correction, including first activation and settings transitions.
evidenceScope: current source and synthetic director selection; no rendered site or hardware benchmark
performance: Fixed slot counts and synthetic selections only; no frame-time result.

action: Correct the Breakwater Spur lamp group's render-frame projection and test its coordinate behavior.
observation: The added regression reproduced the worklight head's global/local mismatch; translating the shared lamp group by negative frame origin keeps all bulbs and lights together, with the expected head position at initial nonzero origin, after rebase and when origin is absent. The three focused tests pass.
decision: Keep existing lamp counts, stage behavior, colors and intensities; make the frame-origin repair in the site presentation owner and leave pool optimization separate.
next: Verify the lit site on the ordinary route and assess the pool alternative with matched imagery and timings.
evidenceScope: source change and focused Three scene-graph regression; no rendered player encounter
performance: No frame-time comparison; the fix is a coordinate correctness change.

action: Compare the Ceres Three-Lamp Corner landmark description with the authored tower and available fixture hooks.
observation: The landmark calls for a three-lamp rig with two dead and one lit but points at the same eight-head worklight package as ordinary towers, without a declared world-site fixture recipe. The warm lamps share one combined primitive per LOD rather than individually bound light materials.
decision: Record a distinct place-specific visual-variation opportunity; do not globally dim the shared worklight or claim an existing per-lamp switch.
next: Inspect the actual landmark on the ordinary route before deciding whether to author a separate damaged crown or adapt its description.
evidenceScope: current authored data and GLB/source topology, not a player-route image
performance: No runtime or GPU measurements; any variation should avoid added draw or light cost where practical.

action: Render and visually inspect the worklight tower at place, side, top, chase and close views through the current isolated renderer.
observation: The place, side and top views preserve a readable open mast, dark machinery base, hazard stripes, red/green markers, eight warm lamp rims and an amber centre. The individual rims merge into a small lit crown in the chase view; the close crop clips the crown. The target-draw report shows nine submissions in each isolated LOD0 shot.
decision: Keep the lit crown, truss silhouette and nav colors intact when testing lower-segment flood geometry. Judge crown shape with place and top views, and do not use the clipped close crop alone.
next: Have the Astra model author export a bounded crown candidate and compare current LOD0, LOD1 and LOD2 in a matched renderer session.
evidenceScope: current isolated GPU-path preview; not a natural player route or verified runtime tier frequency
performance: Nine target draws are from the uncomposed preview only; no frame-time or normal composed draw count was measured.

action: Exercise the actual POI materialization owner for Three-Lamp Corner at full and reduced residency.
observation: The unhidden Ceres landmark is an fx actor at global (-11788,7542) under FULL residency and a dressing row under REDUCED; both resolve the same worklight place id, radius 12, no collision and no NOCTURNE archetype or per-lamp stage data.
decision: Treat this as one specific existing deployment with the ordinary model, not a currently implemented alternate or staged lamp variant.
next: Keep its discovery identity and residency behavior intact if an authored alternative is later selected.
evidenceScope: deterministic isolated world-owner materialization and NOCTURNE resolver, not a rendered gameplay encounter
performance: No draw, frame-time or resident-GPU-resource measurement.

action: Inspect warm-lamp UVs and vertex attributes in the current source and meshopt-compressed release geometry.
observation: The single LOD0 warm-emissive primitive contains eight 248-triangle floodhead groups; its attributes have no vertex-color selection mask. Different groups share exact UV triangles, with up to 144 shared triangles per pair, so the current UV map cannot independently preserve every complete lit head while blacking out arbitrary others.
decision: Reject a simple site-specific emissive-factor change or unmodified UV texture as a complete one-lit/two-dead solution. An authored alternative may use existing dark and warm materials and material-group batching, but actual draw/resource effects must be measured.
next: After the base tower candidate is judged, compare a three-head scratch alternative that keeps one warm lens and two dark lenses without adding material families.
evidenceScope: static source and release LOD0 attribute/UV analysis, not rendered material experimentation
performance: Existing geometry counts only; no material, draw or frame-time comparison.

action: Trace Pigeon Day's Three-Lamp Corner presentation beats and their VFX consumer.
observation: Pigeon Day targets the materialized POI and emits a four-flash sequence plus two transient point-light VFX cues at 15 and 20 seconds on its 600-second loop. The spectacle owner does not alter the tower's emitter materials or expose a persistent lamp-stage input; this loop is not in its resumable-loop allowlist.
decision: Make any baseline one-lit/two-dead geometry static unless a separately scoped, durable stage contract is designed; preserve the existing transient spectacle cues.
next: Review a natural encounter and the readability of beacon/nav indicators before choosing how many other emissive signals the variant should retain.
evidenceScope: current event and VFX source tracing, not a reproduced or rendered event
performance: No cost measurement; avoid adding a permanent real light solely to represent the always-lit lens.
